page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6r.xlarge is an ARM64-based virtual machine instance powered by a dedicated 4-core Ampere Altra processor running at 2.8 GHz. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It operates on a KVM hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps, and the instance does not come with complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average performance for compute-intensive tasks, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests scoring 1824.29 and 7275.05 respectively. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate average throughput for large block operations, reaching 55.26 GB/sec for read-only and 31.38 GB/sec for write operations. However, small block cached memory read bandwidth is weaker at 283.44 GB/sec. The instance exhibits weak performance in Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, as well as in Passmark CPU tests. Cryptographic operations represent a notable bottleneck, with the Passmark CPU encryption test registering a poor score of 649.93.

Given its dedicated ARM64 architecture and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.c6r.xlarge offers a cost-efficient entry point for ARM-native development, testing, and lightweight multi-threaded applications. It is suited for workloads such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 5.91 GB/sec, and database operations, which score in the average range. The instance is also capable of handling small-scale language model inference, delivering 99.43 tokens/sec for text generation with a 135M model. It is less suitable for memory-intensive applications or heavy cryptographic processing.

Equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM and operating on a KVM hypervisor, this instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. It provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Performance benchmarks place the instance in the average tier for multi-core CPU tasks and large-block memory bandwidth, though it exhibits weaker results in single-core processing, small-block memory reads, and cryptographic operations. The ecs.c6r.xlarge is qualitatively cost-efficient for ARM-native development, static web serving, and moderate database operations, but is not recommended for memory-heavy or cryptographically intensive workloads.
